dimensions.assessment: Affects health care and social service providers nationwide who participate in the training program, as well as individuals experiencing or at risk of human trafficking.
dimensions.evidence: The program provides training for health care and social service providers on how to identify and support those who have experienced or are at risk of experiencing human trafficking.

dimensions.assessment: Continues an existing training program without altering its fundamental structure or creating new enforcement mechanisms.
dimensions.evidence: This bill reauthorizes through FY2030 the Stop, Observe, Ask, and Respond (SOAR) to Health and Wellness Training Program

dimensions.assessment: Extends authorization for an existing program through fiscal year 2030, though specific funding amounts are not detailed in the text.
dimensions.evidence: Section 1254(h) of the Public Health Service Act (42 U.S.C. 300d-54(h)) is amended by striking 'fiscal years 2020 through 2024' and inserting 'fiscal years 2026 through 2030'.

dimensions.assessment: Narrow statutory amendment extending the authorization date of a single existing health program.
dimensions.evidence: To amend the Public Health Service Act to reauthorize the Stop, Observe, Ask, and Respond to Health and Wellness Training Program.

dimensions.assessment: Extends program authorization for a fixed five-year period through fiscal year 2030.

missing_information: Specific dollar amounts authorized for the reauthorization period.
importance_detail.rationale: This bill reauthorizes an existing federal training program within the Department of Health and Human Services through fiscal year 2030, continuing training for health care and social service providers on human trafficking identification.
